old: The standard error attached to a bracket is that of usage at a fixed weight, and the bracket's width is set by the grid, so neither says how often a different sample of seeds would select a different bracket. We measured bracket-selection stability by resampling the five seeds with replacement $2000$ times and re-solving each of the $25$ budgets of Figure~\ref{fig:stairs} on each resampled curve (\texttt{run\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.py}, \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.csv}, with the count of every bracket outcome in \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability\_\allowbreak counts.csv}). The reported bracket is recovered in every resample at $19$ budgets and in at least $99$ percent of resamples at $21$. The lowest agreement is $0.789$, at Inspection's lowest budget. In all but one disagreeing resample, the alternative is a neighbouring step of the staircase or, at Tiger's lowest and highest budgets, no bracket at all. Those two Tiger budgets lie about one standard error of usage from the corresponding ends of its usage range.
